quirks.summary: Portal URL and vendor come from PlanIt's directory; neither the vendor nor any retrieval step has been verified against this portal.
quirks.detail: PlanIt reports scraper_type 'Tascomi'. That label is a hint, not a finding - it is recorded elsewhere in this skill as stale at one authority and wrong at another. Fingerprint the portal before choosing a recipe, and set portal.vendor_verified when you have.
quirks.workaround: Run the vendor detection signatures in vendors.json against the portal before applying any recipe.

quirks.summary: WAF signals present (aws-waf) but the landing page served normally.
quirks.detail: Passive at survey time. Not a reason to avoid the automated route; it is a reason to pace properly and to expect a challenge if you do not.

quirks.summary: HTTP 202 with an empty body is the WAF challenge, not an empty result set.
quirks.detail: Measured on 2026-09-16: 13 of the 14 Tascomi installs surveyed answered 202 with AWS WAF markers. This is a property of the product, not of this council.
quirks.workaround: Stop and hand the user the browser route.

bot_protection.behaviour: Every dynamic request answers HTTP 202 with an x-amzn-waf-action challenge header and an empty body. The empty 202 reads as a successful empty result, so branch on the status and header, never on the body.

browser_route.note: Open the register in a browser; the challenge resolves there. No HTTP route exists.

verification.note: Landing-page survey 2026-09-16: HTTP 202; vendor confirmed by fingerprint (tascomi); WAF signals: aws-waf
Landing-page survey: HTTP 202 + AWS WAF challenge headers. Vendor-wide pattern.
